okf_version: "0.2"
title: neon-ducklake
description: "neon-ducklake harvests the NEON Data API into a DuckDB ducklake-extension catalog lake, builds per-site lakes of stacked NEON data with full AVU metadata on the CyVerse Data Store, and records every AVU change in a MESA history. # neon-ducklake

neon-ducklake is a pipeline and a published product. The pipeline harvests the
[NEON Data API](https://data.neonscience.org/data-api/) and NEON's field-site data into
[DuckLake](https://ducklake.select/) lakes on the CyVerse Data Store. The product is the public
collection it writes:

```
https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/
```

Anyone can read it with DuckDB over HTTPS, without an account:

```sql
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs; INSTALL ducklake; LOAD ducklake;
ATTACH 'ducklake:https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/ducklake/neon_catalog.ducklake'
    AS neon (READ_ONLY,
             DATA_PATH 'https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/ducklake/data/',
             OVERRIDE_DATA_PATH true);
SELECT count(*) AS products FROM neon.products;
```

```text
products
202
```

## The datasets

| Dataset | What it holds (measured 2026-11-24) | Card |
|---|---|---|
| Catalog lake | NEON API metadata: 202 products, 81 sites, releases RELEASE-2021 to RELEASE-2026, availability, locations, taxonomy, and an inventory of 3,215,813 non-AOP files (4,034.1 GB). Built 2026-09-27 | [Catalog lake](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/catalog-lake/) |
| Site lakes | Stacked, typed NEON data for one site per lake. SRER and KONZ are published, both as partial sample runs | [Site lakes](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/site-lakes/) |
| AVU history | 104,964 AVU add/delete events with provenance, in plain Parquet under `.mesa/ducklake/` | [AVU history](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/avu-history/) |

[The published collection](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/collection/) explains every path in the collection, including
the history spool (`.mesa/spool/`, `.mesa/spool-done/`).

## Engineering

- [Architecture](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/engineering/architecture/): the two phases and the stages of a site run.
- [How lakes are built and published](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/engineering/building-lakes/): local build, one snapshot
  per build, checksum-verified uploads with the catalog file last, and the history spool.
- [Running the pipeline](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/engineering/running/): install, quick start, full sweep, refresh.
- [Adding a site or product](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/engineering/extending/).
- [Testing and verification](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/engineering/testing/).

## Design records

These are the project's original design documents, kept at their paths.

| Document | Read it when you want to |
|---|---|
| [Design plan](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/PLAN/) | See the approved design: phases, architecture, catalog tables, AVU vocabulary, bulk writer and history, and verification. |
| [Scaling to 81 sites](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/SCALING/) | Understand how the site pipeline scales to all 81 sites: limits and decisions, the orchestrator, resource classes, and measured throughput. |
| [Internal contracts](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/CONTRACTS/) | Change code: the interfaces every module codes against, lake tables and columns, `avu_desired`, uploads and the ontology stores. |
| [Streaming and multi-VM](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/STREAMING/) | Understand the streaming pipeline and the multi-VM contract: chunks, per-chunk stages and return codes, the versioned site lake on the Data Store, spool-only history and the recorder, site claims, journal backups, and the orchestrator. |
| [Runbook](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/RUNBOOK/) | Operate the pipeline: prerequisites, the orchestrator, monitoring, recovery, review, refreshing after a NEON release, eviction, streaming, workers and the recorder. |
| [Workers on DE VMs](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/DE_SANDBOX/) | Run workers on several CyVerse Discovery Environment VMs: roles, setup, secrets without a keyring, the worker, the recorder, stale claims and troubleshooting. |

The [README](https://github.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/blob/main/README.md) and the
[CHANGELOG](https://github.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) are in the
repository root.

### Order of precedence

`PLAN.md` is the approved design as written. `SCALING.md`, `CONTRACTS.md`, `STREAMING.md` and
`RUNBOOK.md` record the decisions made since then. Where they disagree with the plan, they win;
where `STREAMING.md` disagrees with `SCALING.md` or `CONTRACTS.md` about streaming or several VMs,
it wins.

### Scripts

| Script | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `scripts/with-secrets.sh CMD...` | Runs `CMD` with the NEON token and CyVerse credentials: from the login keyring, or from the environment and `~/.irods` on a VM (`NEON_DUCKLAKE_SECRETS=env\|keyring\|auto`). It never prints them. |
| `scripts/full_sweep.sh` | Runs the full sweep safely: preflight, plan and estimate, confirmation, the MESA history recorder (tmux session `neon-recorder`), `neon-ducklake run`, then status. |
| `scripts/sweep_status.sh` | Shows sweep progress: stages, chunks, the working set, the spool backlog and the recorder, the latest sweep log, free disk and the MESA snapshot budget. |
| `scripts/okf_validate.py`, `scripts/gen_llms_txt.py`, `scripts/postbuild_agent_surface.py` | Validate this documentation (OKF v0.2), generate `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`, and add the agent surface to the built site. |

in one file, [`llms-full.txt`](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/llms-full.txt). Every page
is also available as Markdown at its URL plus `index.md`, and as raw source at
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/neon-ducklake/main/docs/<path>.md`. See
[For AI agents](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/about/ai-agents/).

affiliated with NEON, Battelle or NSF. NEON data are licensed CC BY 4.0.

# The published collection

neon-ducklake publishes everything it keeps to one MESA project collection on the CyVerse Data
Store. The collection is public: anyone can read it over HTTPS without an account, a copy, or
this repository.

```
https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/
```

The iRODS path is `/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake` (the default
`NEON_DUCKLAKE_IRODS_ROOT`). To turn any iRODS path in this collection into a URL, prefix it with
`https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon`.

## What is where

Listed with WebDAV `PROPFIND` on 2026-11-24.

| Path | What it is | Written by | Read it with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ducklake/neon_catalog.ducklake`, `ducklake/data/` | The [catalog lake](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/catalog-lake/): NEON API metadata and the file inventory, `ducklake`-extension format | `catalog build`, uploaded by `mirror` (catalog file last) | `ATTACH 'ducklake:...' (READ_ONLY, DATA_PATH ..., OVERRIDE_DATA_PATH true)` |
| `sites/<SITE>/ducklake/` | A [site lake](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/site-lakes/): stacked data tables of one site. Holds `neon_<site>.ducklake` and `data/`; streamed sites add `catalogs/` and `CURRENT` | the site stages; `stream.push_lake` for streamed sites | `ATTACH`, as above |
| `sites/<SITE>/raw/<DP>/<YYYY-MM>/<file>` | NEON's original files, each with its full AVU profile | the upload stage | plain HTTPS GET |
| `sites/<SITE>/reports/` | JSON and CSV stage reports: `plan.json`, `list_summary.json`, `stack_summary.json`, `terms.json`, `verify.json` and others | each stage | `read_json`, or any JSON reader |
| `sites/<SITE>/cards/`, `sites/<SITE>/curation/` | Product and site cards for curation; Opus traces, proposals and `review.md` | `site cards`, `curate`, `validate` | HTTPS GET |
| `sites/<SITE>/.mesa-journal/` | Versioned backups of the site's local journal, behind a `CURRENT` pointer (streamed sites) | `journal push` | internal; for restoring a site on another VM |
| `.mesa/ducklake/snapshot_<id>.parquet` | The [AVU history](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/avu-history/): plain Parquet written by mesa-ducklake, not an extension lake | mesa-ducklake, called by the recorder or by direct-mode history | `read_parquet` |
| `.mesa/spool/<vm>/<batch>.parquet` + `<batch>.json` | AVU history batches a streaming run or worker VM wrote, waiting for the recorder | `avu.history` in spool mode | `read_parquet`, `read_json` |
| `.mesa/spool-done/<vm>/` | Batches the recorder has already recorded into `.mesa/ducklake/`; kept, never deleted | `neon-ducklake recorder` | `read_parquet`, `read_json` |
| `api/runs/<runId>/sealed/` | The sealed NEON API harvest (the catalog build's only input), its manifest and fetch log | `mirror --what api` | HTTPS GET |
| `ref/` | OBO Foundry registry and ontology map exports | `mirror` | HTTPS GET |
| `src/`, `sql/`, `scripts/`, `docs/`, `curation/`, `tests/`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `README.md` | A copy of this repository's code | `mirror --what code` | HTTPS GET |
| `web/index.html` | One HTML file (66,411 bytes, 2026-10-02) | not found in this repository's code | HTTPS GET |

On 2026-11-24, `sites/` held two sites, **SRER** and **KONZ**. `.mesa/spool/sparky-1/` was empty
and `.mesa/spool-done/sparky-1/` held 57 recorded batches. See [AVU history](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/avu-history/) for
how a batch moves from `spool` to `spool-done`.

The project root carries `mesa.enabled=true` and `mesa.project.kind=ducklake`. Each
`sites/<SITE>` collection carries a `mesa.ducklake.catalog` pointer and is never itself
MESA-enabled (README, "Data layout"; the AVUs themselves were not read for this page).

## Two different kinds of "ducklake"

| | Catalog and site lakes | `.mesa/ducklake/` |
|---|---|---|
| Format | DuckDB `ducklake` extension: a `.ducklake` catalog file (a DuckDB database of lake metadata) plus Parquet in `data/` | Plain Parquet, one file per MESA snapshot |
| Catalog | The `.ducklake` file next to the data | The MESA catalog on the recording host; not published |
| Open with | `ATTACH 'ducklake:<url>' AS x (READ_ONLY, DATA_PATH '<url>/data/', OVERRIDE_DATA_PATH true)` | `read_parquet([...])` |
| Holds | NEON metadata, stacked NEON data | AVU add/delete events with provenance |

mesa-ducklake follows the DuckLake *pattern* (a separate catalog plus Parquet files), but it does
not use the `ducklake` extension, so there is no `.ducklake` file to attach. Its Parquet rows carry
their own `project_id`, `snapshot_id`, `ts`, `actor` and `source`, so they can be read without the
catalog. See mesa-ducklake's
[reading a project's history without the catalog](https://github.com/idss-mesa/mesa-ducklake/blob/main/docs/deploy/per-project-storage.md#reading-a-projects-history-without-the-catalog).

## Reading tips

- **DuckDB.** Install the `httpfs` and `ducklake` extensions once (`INSTALL httpfs; INSTALL ducklake;`).
  DuckDB 1.5.5 and 2.0.0 both read the catalog lake (checked 2026-11-24).
- **Python.** `uv run --with duckdb==1.5.5 --with pytz python`; fetching `TIMESTAMPTZ` values into
  Python needs `pytz`.
- **Time zone.** Timestamps are stored in UTC. Run `SET TimeZone = 'UTC';` to print them in UTC.
- **Listing.** HTTP has no glob. List a collection with
  `curl -s -X PROPFIND -H 'Depth: 1' <collection URL>/`.
- **Flaky reads.** The Data Store occasionally returned an empty body on 2026-11-24. Retry, or set
  `SET http_retries = 10;`.
- **Big scans.** For repeated queries over a site lake, copy its `ducklake/` folder (the
  `.ducklake` file and `data/` together) with `gocmd get` or `iget -r` and attach the copy.

# Catalog lake

The catalog lake is NEON Data API metadata harvested into one
[DuckLake](https://ducklake.select/) in DuckDB's `ducklake` extension format. It holds every
NEON data product (AOP included), site, release, availability month, named location with its
history, taxon, sample class, prototype dataset and document, plus an inventory of every
non-AOP basic-package data file. It holds no measurements. For stacked data, see the
[site lakes](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/site-lakes/).

All numbers on this page come from queries run read-only over HTTPS on 2026-11-24.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Location | `https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/ducklake/` (`neon_catalog.ducklake` plus `data/`) |
| Format | DuckLake 1.0 (`ducklake` extension), Parquet with zstd, schema `main` |
| Size | catalog file 4,468,736 bytes; README states about 230 MB of Parquet (not re-measured) |
| Tables | 56 tables and 3 views: 38 tables built from the NEON API harvest (`table_catalog.source`; this includes the `harvest_runs` and `harvest_requests` ledgers), 2 build bookkeeping tables (`catalog_builds`, `table_catalog`), 16 spatial layers, and the views `v_site_inventory`, `v_pair_coverage`, `v_product_summary` |
| Snapshots | One build: snapshot 1, `catalog build 20260927T143926Z`, 2026-09-27 15:30:49 UTC |
| Source | NEON Data API (REST and GraphQL) through neon-mcp's client, harvest run `20260927T143926Z` (complete, 5,048 product x site pairs, 0 failures) |
| NEON releases | RELEASE-2021 to RELEASE-2026, plus PROVISIONAL months |
| Coverage | 202 products (161 non-AOP, 41 AOP), 81 sites, 20 domains, months 2010-12 to 2026-09 |
| File inventory | 3,215,813 files, 4,034.1 GB, 121 products, 81 sites |
| Licence | NEON data and metadata are CC BY 4.0 |

## How to read it

### HTTPS, read-only, no account

This works with DuckDB 1.5.5 and 2.0.0 (both checked on 2026-11-24). `DATA_PATH` plus
`OVERRIDE_DATA_PATH true` replaces the relative `data/` path the build recorded.

```sql
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs; INSTALL ducklake; LOAD ducklake;
SET TimeZone = 'UTC';
ATTACH 'ducklake:https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/ducklake/neon_catalog.ducklake'
    AS neon (READ_ONLY,
             DATA_PATH 'https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/ducklake/data/',
             OVERRIDE_DATA_PATH true);
SELECT count(*) AS products FROM neon.products;
```

```text
products
202
```

The attach took about 2 s. Most queries below took 0.1 to 5 s.

From Python, `uv run --with duckdb==1.5.5 --with pytz python` works. Without `pytz`, fetching a
`TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE` value into Python fails.

### Local copy

Copy `ducklake/neon_catalog.ducklake` and `ducklake/data/` together (for example with `gocmd get`
or `iget -r`) and attach the copy with a local `DATA_PATH`. In a checkout of this repository,
`sql/attach_all.sql` does this from the data root, and `neon_ducklake.catalog_lake.attach_all(con)`
does it from Python. The local-copy route was not re-run for this page.

### Other access paths

- **neon-mcp** does not read this lake. It calls the live NEON Data API, which is the same source
  the lake was harvested from. Use it for data newer than the harvest, and for signed download
  URLs (`neon_list_files`, which needs a NEON API token).
- **The MESA Quack endpoint** does not apply. Quack serves a MESA *history* catalog, not this
  lake, and no public Quack endpoint for this project is documented.
- **mesa-mcp's `mesa_ducklake_*` tools** read the AVU history, not this lake. See
  [AVU history](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/avu-history/).

## Tables

`table_catalog` describes every table and view in the lake: group, key, row count, and source.
Every NEON-derived table also has two bookkeeping columns, `rowHash` (md5 of the row's JSON, used
for upserts) and `loadedRun` (the harvest run that loaded the row). The full column list with types
is in [Catalog lake: column reference](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/catalog-lake-columns/).

```sql
SELECT tableGroup, count(*) AS n_tables, sum(rowCount) AS n_rows
FROM neon.table_catalog
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
```

```text
tableGroup | n_tables | n_rows
availability | 2 | 297354
inventory | 4 | 3504420
meta | 4 | 17560
other | 7 | 136601
products | 8 | 10872
releases | 7 | 966423
sites | 8 | 400669
spatial | 16 | 157082
view | 3 | NULL
```

The main tables, their grain and their keys:

| Table | One row per | Key | Rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| `products` | NEON data product (current `/products`) | `productCode` | 202 |
| `product_releases` | product x release, with the release DOI (`productDoi` is the bare `10.48443/...` DOI) | `productCode, release` | 683 |
| `releases` | NEON release tag | `release` | 6 |
| `release_manifest_months` | product x site x month cell of each release manifest | `release, productCode, siteCode, month` | 918,893 |
| `sites` | NEON field site, with elevation, UTM and `siteProperties` (a MAP, for example `siteProperties['HABITAT']`) | `siteCode` | 81 |
| `domains` | NEON domain | `domainCode` | 20 |
| `locations` | named location (GraphQL `findLocations` over the `/locations` hierarchy) | `locationName` | 379,745 |
| `location_history` | history entry of a CONFIG, TOWER or SITE location | `locationName, historyIndex` | 13,902 |
| `site_products` | current site x product availability (`/sites`) | `siteCode, productCode` | 6,112 |
| `availability_months` | product x site x month: current availability (a release or PROVISIONAL) plus release-only months | `productCode, siteCode, month` | 291,080 |
| `product_site` | product x site pair, with `inventoryScope` (current, release-only, excluded:AOP) and `inventoryStatus` (ok, external, empty, error, missing) | `productCode, siteCode` | 6,274 |
| `site_month_packages` | basic package: product x site x month x release | `productCode, siteCode, month, release` | 283,401 |
| `files` | non-AOP basic-package file; DP0 support files are attributed to the requested DP1 product; `objectUrl` is unsigned | `productCode, siteCode, month, release, name` | 3,215,813 |
| `external_data` | link to data hosted outside NEON | `productCode, siteCode, url` | 158 |
| `taxonomy` | NEON taxon (verbose record; `dwc:`/`gbif:` prefixes stripped; full record as JSON) | `taxonTypeCode, taxonID` | 134,196 |
| `catalog_builds` | catalog build (append-only) | `buildId` | 1 |
| `harvest_runs` | harvest run loaded into the catalog | `runId` | 1 |

The three views, from `sql/catalog_views.sql`:

| View | One row per | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `v_site_inventory` | non-AOP product x site x month, with `release`, `isProvisional`, `isReleaseOnly`, `isExternal`, `fileCount`, `totalBytes` | the months and bytes available for a product at a site; the Phase-2 planner reads it |
| `v_pair_coverage` | non-AOP product x site | cells with files, external or missing, and the first and last month |
| `v_product_summary` | product | status, team, latest release DOI, pair and cell counts, file totals |

### Keys and joins

- Products: `productCode` (for example `DP1.00002.001`) joins `products`, `product_releases`,
  `product_site`, `availability_months`, `files` and the views.
- Sites: `siteCode` (for example `SRER`) joins `sites`, `site_products`, `availability_months`,
  `files`, `locations` and the views. The spatial layers use `siteID`.
- Months are `VARCHAR` `'YYYY-MM'`. `release` is `'RELEASE-YYYY'` or `'PROVISIONAL'`.
- Site lakes use the same `productCode` and `month` values, so a site lake joins the catalog on
  `(productCode, month)` with `siteCode` fixed (see [Site lakes](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/site-lakes/#compare-a-site-lake-with-the-catalog-inventory)).

## Coverage

```sql
SELECT count(*) AS files, count(DISTINCT productCode) AS products,
       count(DISTINCT siteCode) AS sites, min(month) AS first_month,
       max(month) AS last_month, round(sum(size) / 1e9, 1) AS gb
FROM neon.files;
```

```text
files | products | sites | first_month | last_month | gb
3215813 | 121 | 81 | 2010-12 | 2026-09 | 4034.1
```

```sql
SELECT release, isProvisional, isReleaseOnly, count(*) AS n_files
FROM neon.files
GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1;
```

```text
release | isProvisional | isReleaseOnly | n_files
PROVISIONAL | True | False | 428819
RELEASE-2021 | False | True | 12345
RELEASE-2022 | False | True | 26237
RELEASE-2023 | False | True | 345
RELEASE-2024 | False | True | 7851
RELEASE-2025 | False | True | 56508
RELEASE-2026 | False | False | 2683708
```

A release-only file belongs to a month that appears in an earlier release manifest but not in
current availability; its `release` is the newest manifest that contains it.

Other counts measured the same day:

- `products`: 202 rows; `isAop` false for 161 and true for 41; `productStatus` ACTIVE 173,
  FUTURE 29.
- `availability_months`: 159 distinct products, 81 sites, months 2010-12 to 2026-09.
- `v_site_inventory` (non-AOP only): 125 products, 81 sites, 283,401 cells, 3,215,813 files.
- `sites`: 40 CORE and 41 GRADIENT; `siteProperties['HABITAT']` is Terrestrial for 47,
  Aquatic Wadeable Stream for 24, Aquatic Lake for 7 and Aquatic Non-wadeable Stream for 3.
- `files.kind`: data 2,016,986; eml 266,246; readme 266,058; variables 260,943;
  sensor_positions 160,351; categorical_codes 119,429; validation 100,592;
  science_review_flags 20,080; lab 5,128.

## Example queries

### Which months exist for a product at a site

```sql
SELECT month, release, isProvisional, isReleaseOnly, fileCount, totalBytes
FROM neon.v_site_inventory
WHERE productCode = 'DP1.00002.001' AND siteCode = 'SRER'
ORDER BY month DESC
LIMIT 5;
```

```text
month | release | isProvisional | isReleaseOnly | fileCount | totalBytes
2026-08 | PROVISIONAL | True | False | 10 | 14013500
2026-07 | PROVISIONAL | True | False | 10 | 14085588
2026-06 | PROVISIONAL | True | False | 10 | 13631992
2026-05 | PROVISIONAL | True | False | 10 | 14080149
2026-04 | PROVISIONAL | True | False | 10 | 13569169
```

Over all months, that pair has 110 months from 2017-07 to 2026-08, 14 of them PROVISIONAL.
`availability_months` gives the same months for AOP products too.

### From a product to its data files

```sql
SELECT name, kind, tableName, hor, ver, tmi, size
FROM neon.files
WHERE productCode = 'DP1.00002.001' AND siteCode = 'SRER' AND month = '2026-08'
ORDER BY name
LIMIT 3;
```

```text
name | kind | tableName | hor | ver | tmi | size
NEON.D14.SRER.DP1.00002.001.000.010.001.SAAT_1min.2026-08.basic.20260907T191004Z.csv | data | SAAT_1min | 000 | 010 | 001 | 4485203
NEON.D14.SRER.DP1.00002.001.000.010.030.SAAT_30min.2026-08.basic.20260907T191004Z.csv | data | SAAT_30min | 000 | 010 | 030 | 152702
NEON.D14.SRER.DP1.00002.001.000.020.001.SAAT_1min.2026-08.basic.20260907T191004Z.csv | data | SAAT_1min | 000 | 020 | 001 | 4480142
```

`files.objectUrl` holds NEON's storage URL with the signature removed, for example
`https://storage.googleapis.com/neon-publication/NEON.DOM.SITE.DP1.00002.001/SRER/20260801T000000--20260901T000000/basic/<name>`.
That URL returned HTTP 403 on 2026-11-24, so it is an identifier, not a download link. To get the
file:

- if the site and month are in a [site lake](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/site-lakes/), the Data Store copy is public at
  `https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon` + the site lake's `files.irodsPath`;
- otherwise ask the NEON API for a signed URL, for example with neon-mcp's `neon_list_files`
  (needs a NEON API token).

### Which NEON release the lake reflects, and the DOI to cite

```sql
SELECT release, generationDate, productCount, manifestCellCount
FROM neon.releases
ORDER BY release;
```

```text
release | generationDate | productCount | manifestCellCount
RELEASE-2021 | 2021-01-23 02:30:02+00:00 | 106 | 88729
RELEASE-2022 | 2022-01-20 17:39:46+00:00 | 109 | 113326
RELEASE-2023 | 2023-01-27 12:07:53+00:00 | 109 | 135593
RELEASE-2024 | 2024-01-27 00:04:25+00:00 | 109 | 161471
RELEASE-2025 | 2025-01-29 00:07:30+00:00 | 114 | 195631
RELEASE-2026 | 2026-01-23 00:07:49+00:00 | 136 | 224143
```

```sql
SELECT release, productDoi
FROM neon.product_releases
WHERE productCode = 'DP1.00002.001'
ORDER BY release DESC
LIMIT 2;
```

```text
release | productDoi
RELEASE-2026 | 10.48443/p69b-5e50
RELEASE-2025 | 10.48443/hejx-aa82
```

Cite released data at its release DOI. Cite PROVISIONAL data by product and download date (see
NEON's [data policies](https://www.neonscience.org/data-samples/data-policies-citation)).

### The largest non-AOP products

```sql
SELECT productCode, productName, pairsWithFiles, fileCount, round(totalBytes / 1e9, 1) AS gb
FROM neon.v_product_summary
WHERE NOT isAop
ORDER BY totalBytes DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 3;
```

```text
productCode | productName | pairsWithFiles | fileCount | gb
DP1.00094.001 | Soil water content and water salinity | 46 | 405961 | 995.2
DP1.00041.001 | Soil temperature | 46 | 465324 | 897.2
DP4.00200.001 | Bundled data products - eddy covariance | 47 | 15345 | 646.5
```

## Freshness

```sql
SELECT snapshot_id, snapshot_time, author, commit_message
FROM neon.snapshots();
```

```text
snapshot_id | snapshot_time | author | commit_message
0 | 2026-09-27 15:30:49.814570+00:00 | NULL | NULL
1 | 2026-09-27 15:30:49.880350+00:00 | tswetnam | catalog build 20260927T143926Z
```

```sql
SELECT runId, status, startedAt, finishedAt, pairs, failureCount
FROM neon.harvest_runs;
```

```text
runId | status | startedAt | finishedAt | pairs | failureCount
20260927T143926Z | complete | 2026-09-27 14:40:11.442263+00:00 | 2026-09-27 15:22:34.437292+00:00 | 5048 | 0
```

```sql
SELECT min(month) FILTER (WHERE isProvisional) AS first_provisional,
       max(month) FILTER (WHERE isProvisional) AS last_provisional,
       max(month) FILTER (WHERE NOT isProvisional AND NOT isReleaseOnly) AS last_released
FROM neon.availability_months;
```

```text
first_provisional | last_provisional | last_released
2013-06 | 2026-09 | 2025-06
```

- **Built:** 2026-09-27, from one harvest that ran 14:40 to 15:22 UTC that day.
- **NEON state it reflects:** RELEASE-2026 (generated 2026-01-23) plus PROVISIONAL months up to
  2026-09 as the API served them on 2026-09-27. The newest released (RELEASE-2026) month is
  2025-06.
- **How to tell from the data:** `snapshots()` (one build per snapshot), `catalog_builds.builtAt`,
  `harvest_runs`, `max(month)` in `availability_months`, and the newest row of `releases`.
  `catalog_builds.versions` and `.tools` record the code and tool versions of the build
  (DuckDB 1.5.5 for this one).
- **Refresh:** a new build adds one snapshot (`catalog fetch --new`, `catalog seal`,
  `catalog build`, then `mirror --what api,lake`). See
  [Running the pipeline](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/engineering/running/#refresh-after-a-new-neon-release).
  Every release in the lake was generated in late January (2021 to 2026, the `generationDate`
  values above). If NEON keeps that pattern, a RELEASE-2027 would not be in this lake until it is
  rebuilt.

## Known limitations

- **Metadata only.** No measurements. Measurements are in the site lakes, which cover only a
  sample of two sites today.
- **AOP files are not inventoried.** AOP products are in `products`, `product_site`
  (`inventoryScope = 'excluded:AOP'`, 1,824 pairs) and `availability_months`, but `files` and the
  views exclude them.
- **Basic package only.** The inventory lists the basic package, not the expanded one.
- **`objectUrl` is unsigned** and does not download (HTTP 403).
- **External products** (data hosted outside NEON) have no files; their links are in
  `external_data` (158 rows; `product_site.inventoryStatus = 'external'` for 158 pairs).
- **A snapshot in time.** PROVISIONAL months change and can be replaced when NEON releases them.
- **Spatial layers** were copied once from a separate spatial lake (version 90). Their `GEOMETRY`
  columns read without extensions; `ST_*` functions need `INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial;`.
- **DuckDB versions.** The lake was written by DuckDB 1.5.5 and reads in 1.5.5 and 2.0.0. The
  README warns that a lake DuckDB 2.0 has written to can no longer be opened by DuckDB 1.x; that
  will apply once a 2.0 build is published.

# Catalog lake: column reference

This page lists every table and view of the [catalog lake](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/catalog-lake/). The descriptions,
keys and row counts come from the lake's own `table_catalog`; the columns and types come from
`information_schema.columns`. Both were read on 2026-11-24 from snapshot 1 (built 2026-09-27).

Two bookkeeping columns are left out of every table below: `rowHash` (VARCHAR, md5 of the row's
JSON, used by the hash-keyed upsert) and `loadedRun` (VARCHAR, the harvest run that loaded the
row). The 16 spatial tables have neither. Columns keep NEON's camelCase names; tables are
snake_case.

To list the columns of one table yourself:

```sql
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs; INSTALL ducklake; LOAD ducklake;
ATTACH 'ducklake:https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/ducklake/neon_catalog.ducklake'
    AS neon (READ_ONLY,
             DATA_PATH 'https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/ducklake/data/',
             OVERRIDE_DATA_PATH true);
SELECT column_name, data_type
FROM information_schema.columns
WHERE table_catalog = 'neon' AND table_name = 'releases'
ORDER BY ordinal_position;
```

The output below is an excerpt (`...` marks omitted rows); the full list is in the
[`releases`](#releases) section.

```text
column_name | data_type
release | VARCHAR
...
generationDate | TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
...
manifestCellCount | BIGINT
...
```

# Site lakes

A site lake holds the NEON data of one field site, stacked into typed tables with neonUtilities
`stackByTable` semantics, plus tables that describe the files, variables, sensor positions and
taxa. Each site lake is a DuckLake in DuckDB's `ducklake` extension format under
`sites/<SITE>/ducklake/` in the published collection.

!!! warning "Two sites, both partial"

    On 2026-11-24 the Data Store held site lakes for **SRER** and **KONZ** only. Both are sample
    runs, not full sites: the SRER lake holds 1,274 of the 49,885 files the catalog inventory lists
    for SRER, and the KONZ lake holds 1,241 of 54,157. Most products have one or two months. Do
    not use these lakes to answer "all data for site X"; use the
    [catalog lake](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/catalog-lake/) to see what exists, and the lake to read what was stacked.

All numbers on this page come from queries run read-only over HTTPS on 2026-11-24.

## At a glance

| | SRER | KONZ |
|---|---|---|
| Site | Santa Rita Experimental Range NEON, D14, CORE, Terrestrial | Konza Prairie Biological Station NEON, D06, CORE, Terrestrial |
| Catalog file | `sites/SRER/ducklake/neon_srer.ducklake` (10,235,904 bytes) | `sites/KONZ/ducklake/CURRENT` points to `catalogs/neon_konz.0000000919-66a0ae9483-532c94029a3a.ducklake` (12,857,344 bytes); `neon_konz.ducklake` is a copy with the same md5 |
| How it was built | whole-site stages only (commit messages `site list`, `site download`, `stack SRER ...`), 2026-09-27 14:58 to 2026-09-28 04:07 UTC; no versioned catalogs | whole-site stages (snapshots 1 to 705, from 2026-09-28 02:48 UTC), then a streaming run (`stream stack ...`, snapshots 706 to 919, 2026-09-29); versioned catalogs behind `CURRENT` |
| Snapshots | 322 (0 to 321); last at 2026-09-28 04:07:22 UTC | 920 (0 to 919); last at 2026-09-29 16:15:26 UTC |
| Tables | 163: 146 stacked tables (`dp*`) and 17 others | 166: 145 stacked tables and 21 others |
| `files` rows | 1,274 (catalog inventory for SRER: 49,885) | 1,241 (catalog inventory for KONZ: 54,157) |
| `site_months` rows | 120 product-months, 2013-11 to 2026-09, 46 PROVISIONAL | 112 product-months, 2014-06 to 2026-09, 46 PROVISIONAL |
| Verify report | `sites/SRER/reports/verify.json`, 2026-09-28: 12 pass, 1 info | no `verify.json` in `sites/KONZ/reports/` |
| Raw files | `sites/SRER/raw/<DP>/<YYYY-MM>/` (57 product folders) | `sites/KONZ/raw/<DP>/<YYYY-MM>/` (58 product folders) |

The SRER `verify.json` describes the listing as "inventory 3727 site-months (328 external,
link-only; 3279 outside the listed windows, e.g. a --sample run), lake 120".

## How to read it

### HTTPS, read-only, no account

```sql
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs; INSTALL ducklake; LOAD ducklake;
SET TimeZone = 'UTC';
ATTACH 'ducklake:https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/sites/SRER/ducklake/neon_srer.ducklake'
    AS neon_srer (READ_ONLY,
                  DATA_PATH 'https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/sites/SRER/ducklake/data/',
                  OVERRIDE_DATA_PATH true);
ATTACH 'ducklake:https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/sites/KONZ/ducklake/neon_konz.ducklake'
    AS neon_konz (READ_ONLY,
                  DATA_PATH 'https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/sites/KONZ/ducklake/data/',
                  OVERRIDE_DATA_PATH true);
SELECT table_catalog, count(*) AS n_tables
FROM information_schema.tables
WHERE table_catalog IN ('neon_srer', 'neon_konz')
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
```

```text
table_catalog | n_tables
neon_konz | 166
neon_srer | 163
```

Measured times on 2026-11-24 with DuckDB 1.5.5: attaching both lakes took about 6 s, and queries
on one stacked table or on `files` took 1 to 4 s. A scan of a table stored as many tiny Parquet
files is slow: `table_catalog` keeps one file per row, and a `GROUP BY` over the SRER
`table_catalog` (446 files) took 82 s in one run and 17 s in another. For repeated or wide scans, copy the lake first.

`DATA_PATH` plus `OVERRIDE_DATA_PATH true` is required: the writers recorded an absolute local
path (for example `/home/.../sites/SRER/ducklake/data/`) as the lake's data path.

### Which catalog file to attach (KONZ and future streamed sites)

A streamed site keeps one immutable catalog per push in `catalogs/` and a JSON pointer,
`CURRENT`, to the current one. The canonical `neon_<site>.ducklake` is refreshed after the
pointer, for readers that predate versioning. The pipeline's own readers take the pointer's
target when its md5 matches, else the newest versioned catalog that verifies, else the canonical
copy. Read the pointer with DuckDB:

```sql
SELECT catalog, md5, snapshotId, pushedAt
FROM read_json('https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/sites/KONZ/ducklake/CURRENT');
```

```text
catalog | md5 | snapshotId | pushedAt
neon_konz.0000000919-66a0ae9483-532c94029a3a.ducklake | 532c94029a3ac5765425c63de1f97341 | 919 | 2026-09-29 16:16:52.454961
```

On 2026-11-24 the canonical `neon_konz.ducklake` had the same md5 (`532c9402...`), so attaching
either gives snapshot 919. To pin a version, attach
`sites/KONZ/ducklake/catalogs/<catalog>` with the same `DATA_PATH`.

### Local copy

Copy the site's `ducklake/` folder (the `.ducklake` file and `data/` together) with `gocmd get`
or `iget -r`, then attach the copy with its local `data/` as `DATA_PATH`, as `sql/attach_all.sql`
does. `sql/attach_all.sql` also lists HARV, which has no lake on the Data Store; that ATTACH fails.
The local-copy route was not re-run for this page.

### Other access paths

- **neon-mcp** does not read site lakes; it calls the live NEON API.
- **mesa-mcp** has no tool that reads these lakes. Its `mesa_ducklake_*` tools read AVU history.
- **The MESA Quack endpoint** serves a MESA history catalog, not site lakes. None is documented
  for this project.

## Tables

### Stacked data tables

One table per product and NEON table, named
`lower(productCode with '.' replaced by '_') || '__' || lower(tableName)`, for example
`dp1_00002_001__saat_30min` (single aspirated air temperature, 30-minute) or
`dp1_10003_001__brd_countdata` (breeding landbird point counts). Columns are NEON's, typed from
the product's `variables` file (a column with more than 0.1% cast failures stays VARCHAR and is
logged in `cast_errors`), plus `siteID`, `domainID`, `month`, `release`, `publicationDate` and
`sourceFile`. Instrumented-system (IS) tables also get `horizontalPosition`,
`verticalPosition` and `tmi`. Tables with a `uid` keep the newest publication per `uid`. Lab
files go to `<dp>__lab_<table>`; the DP4.00200.001 eddy-covariance HDF5 files go to
`dp4_00200_001__nsae_dp04` plus `h5_attrs`, `h5_datasets` and (KONZ) `h5_objdesc`.

`table_catalog` lists every stacked table with its product, NEON table name, kind, file count,
row count and month range:

```sql
SELECT kind, count(*) AS n_tables, sum(nRows) AS n_rows
FROM neon_srer.table_catalog
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
```

```text
kind | n_tables | n_rows
data | 144 | 12731568
h5 | 1 | 7344
lab | 1 | 2
support | 300 | 28251
```

(`support` rows describe per-product supporting tables such as `variables`; one table can have a
row per product.)

Three example schemas:

`dp1_00002_001__saat_30min`: `startDateTime` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `endDateTime` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `tempSingleMean` DOUBLE, `tempSingleMinimum` DOUBLE, `tempSingleMaximum` DOUBLE, `tempSingleVariance` DOUBLE, `tempSingleNumPts` DOUBLE, `tempSingleExpUncert` DOUBLE, `tempSingleStdErMean` DOUBLE, `finalQF` BIGINT, `siteID` VARCHAR, `domainID` VARCHAR, `month` VARCHAR, `release` VARCHAR, `publicationDate` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `sourceFile` VARCHAR, `horizontalPosition` VARCHAR, `verticalPosition` VARCHAR, `tmi` VARCHAR.

`dp1_10003_001__brd_countdata`: `uid` VARCHAR, `namedLocation` VARCHAR, `domainID` VARCHAR, `siteID` VARCHAR, `plotID` VARCHAR, `plotType` VARCHAR, `pointID` VARCHAR, `startDate` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `boutNumber` BIGINT, `eventID` VARCHAR, `pointCountMinute` BIGINT, `targetTaxaPresent` VARCHAR, `taxonID` VARCHAR, `scientificName` VARCHAR, `taxonRank` VARCHAR, `vernacularName` VARCHAR, `observerDistance` DOUBLE, `detectionMethod` VARCHAR, `visualConfirmation` VARCHAR, `sexOrAge` VARCHAR, `clusterSize` BIGINT, `clusterCode` VARCHAR, `identifiedBy` VARCHAR, `identificationHistoryID` VARCHAR, `month` VARCHAR, `release` VARCHAR, `publicationDate` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `sourceFile` VARCHAR.

`dp4_00200_001__nsae_dp04`: `siteID` VARCHAR, `domainID` VARCHAR, `month` VARCHAR, `release` VARCHAR, `publicationDate` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `sourceFile` VARCHAR, `timeBgn` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `timeEnd` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `fluxCo2Turb` DOUBLE, `qfFinlCo2Turb` BIGINT, `fluxCo2Nsae` DOUBLE, `qfFinlCo2Nsae` BIGINT, `fluxCo2Stor` DOUBLE, `qfFinlCo2Stor` BIGINT, `fluxH2oTurb` DOUBLE, `qfFinlH2oTurb` BIGINT, `fluxH2oNsae` DOUBLE, `qfFinlH2oNsae` BIGINT, `fluxH2oStor` DOUBLE, `qfFinlH2oStor` BIGINT, `fluxTempTurb` DOUBLE, `qfFinlTempTurb` BIGINT, `fluxTempNsae` DOUBLE, `qfFinlTempNsae` BIGINT, `fluxTempStor` DOUBLE, `qfFinlTempStor` BIGINT, `footAngZaxsErth` DOUBLE, `footDistReso` DOUBLE, `footVeloYaxsHorSd` DOUBLE, `footVeloZaxsHorSd` DOUBLE, `footVeloFric` DOUBLE, `footDistZaxsMeasDisp` DOUBLE, `footDistZaxsRgh` DOUBLE, `footDistObkv` DOUBLE, `footParaStbl` DOUBLE, `footDistZaxsAbl` DOUBLE, `footDistXaxs90` DOUBLE, `footDistXaxsMax` DOUBLE, `footDistYaxs90` DOUBLE, `qfFinlFoot` BIGINT.

### Other tables

Column names and types below come from `information_schema.columns` of the KONZ lake.

#### `files`

One row per NEON file downloaded for the site, with download checks and its Data Store path (`irodsPath`). Key `productCode, month, name`. Rows: SRER 1,274, KONZ 1,241.

Columns: `productCode` VARCHAR, `siteCode` VARCHAR, `domainCode` VARCHAR, `month` VARCHAR, `release` VARCHAR, `isProvisional` BOOLEAN, `isReleaseOnly` BOOLEAN, `name` VARCHAR, `size` BIGINT, `md5` VARCHAR, `crc32c` VARCHAR, `kind` VARCHAR, `tableName` VARCHAR, `hor` VARCHAR, `ver` VARCHAR, `tmi` VARCHAR, `publicationTimestamp` TIMESTAMP, `ext` VARCHAR, `localRelPath` VARCHAR, `irodsPath` VARCHAR, `dlMd5` VARCHAR, `md5Verified` BOOLEAN, `storageMd5` VARCHAR, `neonMd5` VARCHAR, `transferVerified` BOOLEAN.

#### `site_months`

One row per product x month the site lake holds, with release and file totals. Key `productCode, month`. Rows: SRER 120, KONZ 112.

Columns: `productCode` VARCHAR, `month` VARCHAR, `release` VARCHAR, `isProvisional` BOOLEAN, `isReleaseOnly` BOOLEAN, `releaseGenerationDate` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `packageGenerationDate` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `fileCount` BIGINT, `totalBytes` BIGINT, `isExternal` BOOLEAN.

#### `external_links`

Links of products hosted outside NEON. Key `productCode, url`. Rows: SRER 3, KONZ 3.

Columns: `productCode` VARCHAR, `url` VARCHAR, `name` VARCHAR, `type` VARCHAR, `monthProbed` VARCHAR, `months` VARCHAR[].

#### `variables`

The latest NEON variables definition per product, table and field (description, units, dataType, pubFormat). Rows: SRER 6,735, KONZ 6,827.

Columns: `productCode` VARCHAR, `tableName` VARCHAR, `fieldName` VARCHAR, `description` VARCHAR, `dataType` VARCHAR, `units` VARCHAR, `downloadPkg` VARCHAR, `pubFormat` VARCHAR, `primaryKey` VARCHAR, `categoricalCodeName` VARCHAR, `sourceFile` VARCHAR, `publicationDate` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE.

#### `variables_history`

Every distinct variables definition, with first and last publication. Rows: SRER 6,995, KONZ 7,070.

Columns: `productCode` VARCHAR, `tableName` VARCHAR, `fieldName` VARCHAR, `description` VARCHAR, `dataType` VARCHAR, `units` VARCHAR, `downloadPkg` VARCHAR, `pubFormat` VARCHAR, `primaryKey` VARCHAR, `categoricalCodeName` VARCHAR, `nFiles` BIGINT, `firstPublication` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `lastPublication` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `firstMonth` VARCHAR, `lastMonth` VARCHAR, `latestSourceFile` VARCHAR.

#### `variables_files`

One row per variables file with its record count. Rows: SRER absent, KONZ 104.

Columns: `productCode` VARCHAR, `month` VARCHAR, `sourceFile` VARCHAR, `publicationDate` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `nVariables` BIGINT.

#### `sensor_positions`

Sensor positions per product and month (`HOR.VER`), with sensor latitude, longitude and elevation derived from the reference location plus offsets. Rows: SRER 317, KONZ 312.

Columns: `productCode` VARCHAR, `month` VARCHAR, `release` VARCHAR, `publicationDate` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `sourceFile` VARCHAR, `HOR.VER` VARCHAR, `sensorLocationID` VARCHAR, `sensorLocationDescription` VARCHAR, `positionStartDateTime` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `positionEndDateTime` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `referenceLocationID` VARCHAR, `referenceLocationIDDescription` VARCHAR, `referenceLocationIDStartDateTime` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `referenceLocationIDEndDateTime` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `xOffset` DOUBLE, `yOffset` DOUBLE, `zOffset` DOUBLE, `pitch` DOUBLE, `roll` DOUBLE, `azimuth` DOUBLE, `locationReferenceLatitude` DOUBLE, `locationReferenceLongitude` DOUBLE, `locationReferenceElevation` DOUBLE, `eastOffset` DOUBLE, `northOffset` DOUBLE, `xAzimuth` DOUBLE, `yAzimuth` DOUBLE, `horizontalPosition` VARCHAR, `verticalPosition` VARCHAR, `sensorLatitude` DOUBLE, `sensorLongitude` DOUBLE, `sensorElevation` DOUBLE, `locationType` VARCHAR, `locationLatitude` DOUBLE, `locationLongitude` DOUBLE, `locationElevationCatalog` DOUBLE, `historyLatitude` DOUBLE, `historyLongitude` DOUBLE, `historyElevation` DOUBLE.

#### `categorical_codes`

Distinct categorical code lists per product. Rows: SRER 7,650, KONZ 7,711.

Columns: `productCode` VARCHAR, `name` VARCHAR, `pubCode` VARCHAR, `description` VARCHAR, `startDate` VARCHAR, `endDate` VARCHAR, `nRecords` BIGINT, `nFiles` BIGINT, `firstMonth` VARCHAR, `lastMonth` VARCHAR, `latestSourceFile` VARCHAR, `latestPublication` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE.

#### `validation`

Distinct validation rules per product. Rows: SRER 6,332, KONZ 6,363.

Columns: `productCode` VARCHAR, `table` VARCHAR, `fieldName` VARCHAR, `description` VARCHAR, `dataType` VARCHAR, `units` VARCHAR, `parserToCreate` VARCHAR, `entryValidationRulesParser` VARCHAR, `entryValidationRulesForm` VARCHAR, `nRecords` BIGINT, `nFiles` BIGINT, `firstMonth` VARCHAR, `lastMonth` VARCHAR, `latestSourceFile` VARCHAR, `latestPublication` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE.

#### `science_review_flags`

Distinct science review flags per product. Rows: SRER absent, KONZ 9.

Columns: `productCode` VARCHAR, `srfID` VARCHAR, `startDateTime` VARCHAR, `endDateTime` VARCHAR, `domainID` VARCHAR, `siteID` VARCHAR, `dpID` VARCHAR, `fieldName` VARCHAR, `horizontalPosition` VARCHAR, `verticalPosition` VARCHAR, `srfValue` VARCHAR, `srfValueJustification` VARCHAR, `createDateTime` VARCHAR, `lastUpdateDateTime` VARCHAR, `nRecords` BIGINT, `nFiles` BIGINT, `firstMonth` VARCHAR, `lastMonth` VARCHAR, `latestSourceFile` VARCHAR, `latestPublication` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE.

#### `eml_index`

One row per EML metadata file, with its coverage dates. Rows: SRER 111, KONZ 106.

Columns: `productCode` VARCHAR, `month` VARCHAR, `release` VARCHAR, `sourceFile` VARCHAR, `publicationDate` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `size` BIGINT, `md5` VARCHAR, `md5Verified` BOOLEAN, `localRelPath` VARCHAR, `emlStart` DATE, `emlEnd` DATE.

#### `readme_index`

One row per readme file. Rows: SRER 111, KONZ 106.

Columns: `productCode` VARCHAR, `month` VARCHAR, `release` VARCHAR, `sourceFile` VARCHAR, `publicationDate` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `size` BIGINT, `md5` VARCHAR, `md5Verified` BOOLEAN, `localRelPath` VARCHAR.

#### `file_stats`

One row per stacked data file: row count, time range, finalQF fail percentage, plots, protocol versions, taxon count. Rows: SRER 774, KONZ 752.

Columns: `sourceFile` VARCHAR, `productCode` VARCHAR, `tableName` VARCHAR, `lakeTable` VARCHAR, `month` VARCHAR, `rowCount` BIGINT, `timeMin` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `timeMax` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `timeColumn` VARCHAR, `qfFailPct` DOUBLE, `plotIDs` VARCHAR[], `plotCount` BIGINT, `protocolVersions` VARCHAR[], `taxonCount` BIGINT, `hor` VARCHAR, `ver` VARCHAR, `tmi` VARCHAR.

#### `file_taxa`

Taxa observed per data file, with record counts. Rows: SRER 438, KONZ 624.

Columns: `sourceFile` VARCHAR, `productCode` VARCHAR, `tableName` VARCHAR, `taxonID` VARCHAR, `scientificName` VARCHAR, `taxonRank` VARCHAR, `vernacularName` VARCHAR, `nRecords` BIGINT.

#### `table_catalog`

One row per table the stacker built: product, NEON table name, kind (data, lab, h5, support), files, rows, columns, months, input fingerprint. Rows: SRER 446, KONZ 454.

Columns: `tableName` VARCHAR, `productCode` VARCHAR, `neonTable` VARCHAR, `kind` VARCHAR, `nFiles` BIGINT, `nRows` BIGINT, `nColumns` BIGINT, `firstMonth` VARCHAR, `lastMonth` VARCHAR, `timeColumn` VARCHAR, `inputSha256` VARCHAR, `builtAt` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `nTypedColumns` BIGINT, `nVarcharColumns` BIGINT, `rowsBeforeDedup` BIGINT, `dedupRemoved` BIGINT.

#### `schema_drift`

One row per header group of a data, lab or sensor_positions table. Rows: SRER 171, KONZ 167.

Columns: `productCode` VARCHAR, `tableName` VARCHAR, `lakeTable` VARCHAR, `headerSha1` VARCHAR, `nColumns` BIGINT, `nFiles` BIGINT, `firstMonth` VARCHAR, `lastMonth` VARCHAR, `columns` VARCHAR[], `missingVsUnion` VARCHAR[], `notInVariables` VARCHAR[], `builtAt` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `unknownColumns` VARCHAR[], `firstPublication` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `lastPublication` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE.

#### `cast_errors`

Columns that stayed VARCHAR because more than 0.1% of values failed to cast. Rows: SRER 0, KONZ 0.

Columns: `productCode` VARCHAR, `tableName` VARCHAR, `neonTable` VARCHAR, `columnName` VARCHAR, `targetType` VARCHAR, `nonNull` BIGINT, `failures` BIGINT, `failPct` DOUBLE, `action` VARCHAR, `samples` VARCHAR[], `builtAt` TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE.

#### `stack_file_counts`

Records per source file counted by the streaming stacker. Rows: SRER absent, KONZ 61,610.

Columns: `productCode` VARCHAR, `scope` VARCHAR, `groupKey` VARCHAR, `sourceFile` VARCHAR, `nFiles` BIGINT, `nRecords` BIGINT, `nFailures` BIGINT.

#### `h5_attrs`

Attributes of the DP4.00200.001 HDF5 files. Rows: SRER 105, KONZ 42.

Columns: `productCode` VARCHAR, `sourceFile` VARCHAR, `month` VARCHAR, `path` VARCHAR, `attr` VARCHAR, `value` VARCHAR.

#### `h5_datasets`

Datasets of the DP4.00200.001 HDF5 files (path, shape, dtype, unit). Rows: SRER 13,715, KONZ 5,646.

Columns: `productCode` VARCHAR, `sourceFile` VARCHAR, `month` VARCHAR, `path` VARCHAR, `shape` VARCHAR, `nRows` BIGINT, `dtype` VARCHAR, `fields` VARCHAR[], `unit` VARCHAR.

#### `h5_objdesc`

The `/objDesc` term dictionary of the HDF5 files. Rows: SRER absent, KONZ 1,038.

Columns: `productCode` VARCHAR, `month` VARCHAR, `sourceFile` VARCHAR, `term` VARCHAR, `description` VARCHAR.

## Keys and joins

- `files` is keyed by `productCode, month, name`; `site_months` by `productCode, month`.
- Every stacked table carries `month`, `release` and `sourceFile`. `sourceFile` equals
  `files.name` and `file_stats.sourceFile`, so a row can be traced to its NEON file and its Data
  Store copy.
- `variables` joins a stacked table's columns on `productCode`, `tableName` (NEON's table name,
  for example `SAAT_30min`) and `fieldName`, and gives description and units.
- The site code is fixed per lake. To join the catalog lake, use `productCode` and `month` with
  `siteCode = '<SITE>'`.

## Example queries

### Which months the lake holds for a product

```sql
SELECT productCode, month, release, isProvisional, fileCount
FROM neon_srer.site_months
WHERE productCode = 'DP1.00002.001'
ORDER BY month;
```

```text
productCode | month | release | isProvisional | fileCount
DP1.00002.001 | 2019-05 | RELEASE-2026 | False | 10
DP1.00002.001 | 2024-05 | RELEASE-2026 | False | 10
DP1.00002.001 | 2024-06 | RELEASE-2026 | False | 10
DP1.00002.001 | 2025-06 | RELEASE-2026 | False | 10
DP1.00002.001 | 2026-08 | PROVISIONAL | True | 10
```

The catalog lists 110 months for the same product at SRER.

### Daily mean air temperature, with units

```sql
SELECT verticalPosition, date_trunc('day', startDateTime) AS day,
       round(avg(tempSingleMean), 2) AS mean_c, count(*) AS n
FROM neon_srer.dp1_00002_001__saat_30min
WHERE month = '2026-08' AND finalQF = 0
GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY day, verticalPosition
LIMIT 3;
```

```text
verticalPosition | day | mean_c | n
010 | 2026-08-01 00:00:00+00:00 | 32.59 | 48
020 | 2026-08-01 00:00:00+00:00 | 32.3 | 48
030 | 2026-08-01 00:00:00+00:00 | 32.41 | 48
```

Days are UTC days. `finalQF = 0` keeps records that passed NEON's quality assessment:

```sql
SELECT fieldName, units, description
FROM neon_srer.variables
WHERE productCode = 'DP1.00002.001' AND tableName = 'SAAT_30min'
  AND fieldName IN ('tempSingleMean', 'finalQF')
ORDER BY fieldName;
```

```text
fieldName | units | description
finalQF | NULL | Quality flag indicating whether a data product has passed or failed an overall assessment of its quality, detailed in NEON.DOC.001113 (1=fail, 0=pass)
tempSingleMean | celsius | Arithmetic mean of single aspirated air temperature
```

### Taxa observed

```sql
SELECT taxonID, scientificName, vernacularName, sum(nRecords) AS n
FROM neon_konz.file_taxa
WHERE productCode = 'DP1.10003.001'
GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY n DESC
LIMIT 3;
```

```text
taxonID | scientificName | vernacularName | n
DICK | Spiza americana | Dickcissel | 272
EAME | Sturnella magna | Eastern Meadowlark | 135
BHCO | Molothrus ater | Brown-headed Cowbird | 100
```

### From a row to its file on the Data Store

```sql
SELECT name, 'https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon' || irodsPath AS url, size, md5Verified
FROM neon_srer.files
WHERE productCode = 'DP1.00002.001' AND tableName = 'SAAT_30min' AND month = '2026-08'
ORDER BY name
LIMIT 1;
```

```text
name | url | size | md5Verified
NEON.D14.SRER.DP1.00002.001.000.010.030.SAAT_30min.2026-08.basic.20260907T191004Z.csv | https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/sites/SRER/raw/DP1.00002.001/2026-08/NEON.D14.SRER.DP1.00002.001.000.010.030.SAAT_30min.2026-08.basic.20260907T191004Z.csv | 152702 | True
```

That URL returned HTTP 200 on 2026-11-24. Each file on the Data Store also carries AVUs (see
[AVU history](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/avu-history/)).

### Compare a site lake with the catalog inventory

This joins the site lake with the [catalog lake](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/catalog-lake/); attach the catalog as `neon`
first.

```sql
ATTACH 'ducklake:https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/ducklake/neon_catalog.ducklake'
    AS neon (READ_ONLY,
             DATA_PATH 'https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/ducklake/data/',
             OVERRIDE_DATA_PATH true);
SELECT i.productCode,
       sum(i.fileCount) AS inventory_files,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM neon_srer.files f WHERE f.productCode = i.productCode) AS lake_files
FROM neon.v_site_inventory i
WHERE i.siteCode = 'SRER' AND i.productCode IN ('DP1.00002.001', 'DP1.10003.001')
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
```

```text
productCode | inventory_files | lake_files
DP1.00002.001 | 1100 | 50
DP1.10003.001 | 97 | 13
```

## Freshness

```sql
SELECT 'SRER' AS site, max(snapshot_id) AS last_snapshot, max(snapshot_time) AS last_change
FROM neon_srer.snapshots()
UNION ALL
SELECT 'KONZ', max(snapshot_id), max(snapshot_time) FROM neon_konz.snapshots()
ORDER BY site;
```

```text
site | last_snapshot | last_change
KONZ | 919 | 2026-09-29 16:15:26.615633+00:00
SRER | 321 | 2026-09-28 04:07:22.695171+00:00
```

- **Built:** SRER from 2026-09-27 to 2026-09-28 and KONZ from 2026-09-28 to 2026-09-29 (UTC). Neither has changed since.
- **NEON state:** files were listed against the catalog lake built on 2026-09-27
  (RELEASE-2026 plus PROVISIONAL months); each row's `release` and `publicationDate` say which
  NEON publication it came from.
- **How to tell from the data:** `snapshots()` (every stage commits one snapshot with a message
  such as `stream stack KONZ DP4.00200.001__2025-06_2026-08 h5`), `table_catalog.builtAt`, and for
  streamed sites the `pushedAt` in `CURRENT`.
- **Refresh:** re-run the site from `list` after a catalog refresh
  (`neon-ducklake run SITE --from-stage list`); see
  [Running the pipeline](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/engineering/running/#refresh-after-a-new-neon-release).

## Known limitations

- **Two sites, sampled.** See the warning at the top. The full 81-site sweep had not been
  published as of 2026-11-24.
- **Schemas differ between the two lakes.** KONZ has `h5_objdesc`, `science_review_flags`,
  `stack_file_counts` and `variables_files`; SRER does not. Stacked tables exist only for the
  products and tables the run reached.
- **AOP excluded, basic package only,** as in the catalog inventory.
- **Times are UTC.** `TIMESTAMPTZ` columns are stored in UTC; set `TimeZone = 'UTC'` to print them
  that way.
- **Fragmented small tables** (`table_catalog`, `schema_drift`) are slow to scan over HTTPS.
- **DuckDB versions.** These lakes were written by DuckDB 1.5.x and read with 1.5.5. After the
  pipeline's move to DuckDB 2.0, lakes it writes will need DuckDB 2.0 to read.

# AVU history

Every AVU (attribute, value, unit) that neon-ducklake writes on the Data Store is also recorded
as an event in the project's MESA history. [mesa-ducklake](https://github.com/idss-mesa/mesa-ducklake)
writes that history as plain Parquet files in the project's `.mesa/ducklake/` collection. Each
row is one `add` or `delete` of one AVU on one path at one time, with its provenance.

All numbers on this page come from the published files, read on 2026-11-24.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Location | `https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/.mesa/ducklake/snapshot_<id>.parquet` |
| Files | `snapshot_5` to `snapshot_10` (six files, 1,086,864 bytes in total) |
| Format | Plain Parquet, one file per MESA snapshot. **Not** a `ducklake`-extension lake: there is no `.ducklake` catalog file here |
| Catalog | The MESA catalog (`$MESA_HOME/ducklake/catalog.duckdb`) on the host that ran the recorder. It is not published |
| Rows | 104,964 events on 11,393 distinct paths, one `project_id` (`8a83b1f3-e50f-4530-92ed-4135985a4761`), one actor |
| Coverage | paths under `sites/KONZ` (63,680 rows), `sites/SRER` (41,239) and `ref` (45). No rows for the project root, `ducklake/` or other Phase-1 targets |
| Time range | 2026-09-28 01:49 UTC to 2026-10-04 19:43 UTC |
| Writers | `source` is always `neon-ducklake:site.avus` or one of its sub-sources (`.curation`, `.datacite`, `.envo`, `.ncbitaxon`, `.uo`) |

## How history reaches `.mesa/ducklake/`

The history has two paths in, chosen by `NEON_DUCKLAKE_HISTORY_MODE`:

1. **Journal.** Each AVU the bulk writer applies to iRODS is journaled locally first
   (`work/state.sqlite`): intent, applied, then recorded.
2. **Direct mode** (the default for `--no-stream` runs). The applying host records journal rows
   straight into the MESA catalog, in batches of up to 250,000 rows, one snapshot per batch, under
   the MESA catalog's single-writer lock.
3. **Spool mode** (every streaming run, and every worker VM). The run writes each batch as
   `<batch_id>.parquet` plus a `<batch_id>.json` manifest, uploads both checksum-verified to
   `.mesa/spool/<vm>/` (Parquet first, manifest last) and never opens the MESA catalog.
4. **Recorder.** `neon-ducklake recorder --watch` runs on the one host that owns the MESA catalog.
   Each pass lists `.mesa/spool/*/`, skips batches already in a committed snapshot, and coalesces
   the rest, in order, into groups of at most 250,000 rows. A group is recorded when it holds at
   least 200,000 rows, its oldest batch is older than 12 hours, or `--flush` is given. Each batch
   is checked against its manifest (sha256 and row count), and rows already recorded under another
   batch id are skipped. Each group becomes one snapshot with the note
   `neon-ducklake spool batch=<id>[,<id>...] n=<batches> rows=<rows>`.
5. **mesa-ducklake** writes the snapshot's Parquet to its local cache, pushes it to
   `.mesa/ducklake/snapshot_<id>.parquet` with a checksum check, and only then commits the
   snapshot in its catalog (push-before-commit).
6. After the commit the recorder moves the batch's two files to `.mesa/spool-done/<vm>/`.
   Spool files are never deleted. A batch whose Parquet does not match its manifest stays in
   `.mesa/spool/<vm>/`.

What the collection showed on 2026-11-24:

- `.mesa/spool/sparky-1/` was empty: no batch was waiting.
- `.mesa/spool-done/sparky-1/` held 57 batches (114 files), all with `scope` KONZ, created
  2026-09-29 13:44 to 2026-10-04 19:43 UTC. Their manifests sum to 63,682 rows, which equals the
  row count of `snapshot_10`. So the recorder coalesced those 57 KONZ batches into snapshot 10.
- Snapshots 5 to 9 hold SRER and `ref` rows from 2026-09-28 and match no spool batch. That fits
  direct mode, which SRER's whole-site run used by default; the MESA catalog notes that would
  confirm it are not published.

A spool batch's Parquet has the AVU columns plus `batch_id`, `scope` (the site), `vm` and
`journal_id`, and no `project_id`, `snapshot_id`, `via_ticket` or `rule_invocation`. Its manifest
holds `format` (`neon-ducklake-spool/1`), `batchId`, `scope`, `vm`, `host`, `rows`, `paths`,
`sha256`, `md5`, `bytes`, `createdAt`, `actor` and `journalIds`.

## Columns

The snapshot files have the 13 columns of mesa-ducklake's `avu_changes` fact table:

| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | VARCHAR (UUID) | The MESA project; one value for the whole neon-ducklake collection |
| `snapshot_id` | BIGINT | The MESA snapshot this event belongs to; equals the `<id>` in the file name |
| `irods_path` | VARCHAR | Full Data Store path the AVU is bound to |
| `target_type` | VARCHAR | `collection` or `data_object` here |
| `attribute` | VARCHAR | AVU attribute, for example `neon.release`, `datacite.title`, `ncbitaxon.<taxon>` |
| `value` | VARCHAR | AVU value |
| `unit` | VARCHAR | AVU unit; often a CURIE or DOI, for example `doi:10.48443/p69b-5e50` on `neon.release` |
| `op` | VARCHAR | `add` or `delete` |
| `actor` | VARCHAR | The iRODS user who made the change |
| `ts` | TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE | When the change was applied (UTC) |
| `source` | VARCHAR | The writer, here `neon-ducklake:site.avus[.<sub>]` |
| `via_ticket` | VARCHAR | iRODS ticket used, if any; NULL in every row here |
| `rule_invocation` | VARCHAR | iRODS rule that emitted the change, if any; NULL in every row here |

The AVU vocabulary itself (`neon.*`, `dc.*`, `datacite.*`, `mesa.*`, `provenance.*`, and
ontology attributes such as `uo.*`, `ncbitaxon.*`, `envo.*`) is defined in the
[design plan](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/PLAN/) and its amendments in [CONTRACTS](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/CONTRACTS/).

## How to read it

### HTTPS with DuckDB, no catalog

HTTP has no directory glob, so list the files by name. Snapshot numbers have gaps because the
MESA catalog numbers snapshots across all of its projects. To list what exists, send a WebDAV
`PROPFIND` (for example `curl -s -X PROPFIND -H 'Depth: 1' <collection URL>`).

```sql
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
SET TimeZone = 'UTC';
SET http_retries = 10;
SET VARIABLE base = 'https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/.mesa/ducklake/';
SELECT snapshot_id, count(*) AS n, min(ts) AS first_ts, max(ts) AS last_ts
FROM read_parquet(list_transform([5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10],
                                 i -> getvariable('base') || 'snapshot_' || i || '.parquet'))
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
```

```text
snapshot_id | n | first_ts | last_ts
5 | 496 | 2026-09-28 01:49:19.151720+00:00 | 2026-09-28 01:49:33.998472+00:00
6 | 498 | 2026-09-28 01:49:24.453661+00:00 | 2026-09-28 01:49:40.864431+00:00
7 | 1536 | 2026-09-28 01:49:19.966993+00:00 | 2026-09-28 01:49:42.987872+00:00
8 | 433 | 2026-09-28 01:52:42.204252+00:00 | 2026-09-28 01:52:48.231917+00:00
9 | 38319 | 2026-09-28 04:29:00.540246+00:00 | 2026-09-28 04:30:25.162560+00:00
10 | 63682 | 2026-09-29 13:43:14.301568+00:00 | 2026-10-04 19:43:34.369538+00:00
```

On 2026-11-24 the Data Store sometimes answered a request for one of these files with zero bytes,
and DuckDB failed with "No magic bytes found at end of file". The run with
`SET http_retries = 10` succeeded; whether the setting caused that is not proven. Retrying the
query, or downloading the files first with `curl`, also works.

### The current AVU set of a path

This is mesa-ducklake's effective-AVU rule: for each `(attribute, value, unit)` take the latest
event, ordered by `ts` then `snapshot_id`, and keep it if it is an `add`. Partition on the whole
triple, never on the attribute alone, because iRODS allows several values per attribute.

```sql
WITH h AS (
    SELECT * FROM read_parquet(list_transform([5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10],
                                              i -> getvariable('base') || 'snapshot_' || i || '.parquet'))
), events AS (
    SELECT attribute, value, unit, op,
           row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY attribute, value, unit ORDER BY ts DESC, snapshot_id DESC) AS rn
    FROM h
    WHERE irods_path = '/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/sites/SRER/raw/DP1.00002.001'
)
SELECT attribute, value, unit
FROM events
WHERE rn = 1 AND op = 'add' AND attribute IN ('neon.release', 'neon.fileCount', 'neon.siteMonths')
ORDER BY attribute;
```

```text
attribute | value | unit
neon.fileCount | 50 | count
neon.release | RELEASE-2026 | doi:10.48443/p69b-5e50
neon.siteMonths | 5 | count
```

For the set at an earlier time, add a `ts <=` filter. Snapshot 9 replaced `neon.fileCount` 40
with 50 at 2026-09-28 04:29:38 UTC, so the set as of 02:00 UTC that day still shows 40:

```sql
WITH h AS (
    SELECT * FROM read_parquet(list_transform([5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10],
                                              i -> getvariable('base') || 'snapshot_' || i || '.parquet'))
), events AS (
    SELECT attribute, value, unit, op,
           row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY attribute, value, unit ORDER BY ts DESC, snapshot_id DESC) AS rn
    FROM h
    WHERE irods_path = '/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/sites/SRER/raw/DP1.00002.001'
      AND ts <= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-09-28 02:00:00+00'
)
SELECT attribute, value, unit
FROM events
WHERE rn = 1 AND op = 'add' AND attribute IN ('neon.release', 'neon.fileCount', 'neon.siteMonths')
ORDER BY attribute;
```

```text
attribute | value | unit
neon.fileCount | 40 | count
neon.release | RELEASE-2026 | doi:10.48443/p69b-5e50
neon.siteMonths | 4 | count
```

### Who wrote what

```sql
SELECT source, op, target_type, count(*) AS n
FROM read_parquet(list_transform([5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10],
                                 i -> getvariable('base') || 'snapshot_' || i || '.parquet'))
GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY n DESC
LIMIT 5;
```

```text
source | op | target_type | n
neon-ducklake:site.avus | add | data_object | 81581
neon-ducklake:site.avus.datacite | add | collection | 10806
neon-ducklake:site.avus | add | collection | 7941
neon-ducklake:site.avus.uo | add | collection | 2423
neon-ducklake:site.avus.ncbitaxon | add | data_object | 1065
```

### A recorded spool batch

```sql
SELECT batchId, scope, vm, rows, createdAt
FROM read_json('https://data.cyverse.org/dav-anon/iplant/home/tswetnam/neon-ducklake/.mesa/spool-done/sparky-1/02df8245-d193-4ced-bcdf-b7cb56ee70fa.json');
```

```text
batchId | scope | vm | rows | createdAt
02df8245-d193-4ced-bcdf-b7cb56ee70fa | KONZ | sparky-1 | 181 | 2026-09-29 15:21:42.549759
```

### Through MESA tools

mesa-mcp's `mesa_ducklake_history` and `mesa_ducklake_time_travel` tools read this history through
the MESA catalog the server is configured with. They work only where the project is registered in
that catalog, which today is the MESA install of the host that ran the recorder. Anonymous readers
should use `read_parquet` as above. No public MESA Quack endpoint for this catalog is documented.

## Freshness

- The newest event is at 2026-10-04 19:43:34 UTC (`snapshot_10`). The spool was empty on
  2026-11-24, so no recorded change was waiting.
- The history grows with every pipeline run that writes AVUs. A new snapshot appears as a new
  `snapshot_<id>.parquet`; existing files are never rewritten.
- How to tell from the data: the largest `snapshot_id` and `max(ts)`, and the newest files in
  `.mesa/spool-done/<vm>/`.

## Known limitations

- **No catalog.** Without the MESA catalog you cannot see snapshot notes (batch ids), and you
  cannot tell whether a file's snapshot was committed. mesa-ducklake pushes a snapshot's Parquet
  before it commits the snapshot, so a crash between the two can leave a file whose snapshot is
  later committed by recovery, or marked `failed`. The six files here all predate 2026-10-05.
- **Coverage.** Only site subtrees and `ref` are in these files. The Phase-1 catalog AVUs are not;
  why is not recorded here.
- **Partial sites.** The history covers the AVUs of the SRER and KONZ sample runs only.
- **AVUs that other tools write** (for example `imeta` by hand) are not in this history unless a
  MESA rule or tool recorded them.

# Architecture

neon-ducklake is a Python 3.11 package (`src/neon_ducklake/`, CLI `neon-ducklake`) that builds two
kinds of DuckLake from the NEON Data API and publishes them, with full AVU metadata, as one MESA
project on the CyVerse Data Store. It is research software from the University of New Mexico and
is not affiliated with NEON, Battelle or NSF.

## Two phases

- **Phase 1, the catalog lake.** `catalog fetch` harvests the NEON Data API (REST and GraphQL,
  through neon-mcp's `NeonClient`, in process) into landings under `api/runs/<runId>/`.
  `catalog seal` bundles them into `sealed/`, the build's only input. `catalog build` flattens
  them into `ducklake/neon_catalog.ducklake` in one snapshot. No bulk data is downloaded. See
  [Catalog lake](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/catalog-lake/).
- **Phase 2, site subtrees.** For each site, `neon-ducklake run SITE` lists every non-AOP
  basic-package file (including PROVISIONAL and release-only months), downloads it, stacks the
  tables into `sites/<SITE>/ducklake/neon_<site>.ducklake`, maps taxa, units and biomes to
  ontology terms, curates product terms with Claude Opus, writes AVUs on every collection and
  file, uploads everything to the Data Store and records the AVUs in MESA history. See
  [Site lakes](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/site-lakes/) and [AVU history](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/avu-history/).

The catalog lake's `v_site_inventory` view plans each site: one row per non-AOP product x site x
month with file counts and bytes.

```
                         NEON Data API (REST + GraphQL, API token)
                                          |
                    neon-mcp NeonClient, in-process (rate-limited, retried)
               +--------------------------+-----------------------------+
      Phase 1  | catalog fetch/seal/build               Phase 2         | run SITE...
               v                                                        v
+----------------------------------+  v_site_inventory  +------------------------------------------+
| catalog lake (DuckLake)          | -----------------> | site lakes, one per site (DuckLake)      |
| ducklake/neon_catalog.ducklake   |  plans each site   | sites/<SITE>/ducklake/neon_<site>.duck.. |
+----------------------------------+                    +------------------------------------------+
               |  mirror + chunk upload: checksum-verified puts; local copies deleted after verify
               v
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| CyVerse Data Store  /iplant/home/<user>/neon-ducklake   (one MESA project, mesa.enabled=true)      |
|   AVUs on every collection and data object (journaled bulk writer)                                  |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
               |  history spool (.mesa/spool/<vm>/) -> recorder: coalesced, <= 250,000 rows/snapshot
               v
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| MESA AVU history (mesa-ducklake): catalog on the recorder host; Parquet in .mesa/ducklake/          |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

(Simplified from the README's diagram.)

## Stages of a site run

`neon-ducklake run` **streams** each site by default ([STREAMING](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/STREAMING/)):

| Stage | Does |
|---|---|
| restore | Restores the site's journal and site lake from the Data Store when another VM worked on the site |
| plan, list | Previews the site from `v_site_inventory`; lists files per product with NEON `POST /data/query` |
| chunk-plan | Splits the listed files into chunks: one product, ascending months, at most 8 GB each |
| chunks | Per chunk, pipelined: download, stack (incremental), AVUs, upload (raw files, then the site lake), apply, history (spooled), verify against the Data Store, delete the local files |
| finalize | Terms, cards, curation, the site, product and lake AVUs, the final upload, apply, history, a metadata-level verify |
| cleanup | Deletes the local site-lake data, cards and curation once their Data Store copies are checked |

With `--no-stream` the orchestrator runs 13 whole-site stages: plan, list, download, stack,
terms, cards, curate, validate, upload, apply, record, verify and evict. Each belongs to a resource
class (local, net-in, cpu, llm, net-out, irods-meta, mesa), so different sites can overlap. The
SRER lake was built this way; KONZ was built whole-site and then streamed.

Every stage is idempotent, resumable and safe to kill. A stage that hits a transient condition
exits 4 and is retried with backoff. Several CyVerse Discovery Environment VMs can stream
different sites at once; they coordinate only through the Data Store (site claims, journal
backups, the history spool). See [Workers on DE VMs](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/DE_SANDBOX/).

## Layout

Local (`NEON_DUCKLAKE_ROOT`, default the checkout):

```
src/ tests/ sql/ scripts/ docs/        code (git)
curation/                              prompts, MCP config template, generic/<DP>.validated.json (git)
ref/                                   OBO Foundry registry, ontology_maps/*.parquet exports (git)
api/runs/<runId>/{raw,stage,sealed}/   harvest landings and sealed bundles; api/LATEST
ducklake/neon_catalog.ducklake, data/  Phase-1 catalog lake
sites/<SITE>/raw/<DP>/<YYYY-MM>/<file> NEON files (deleted once verified on the Data Store)
sites/<SITE>/ducklake/                 neon_<site>.ducklake + data/, the per-site lake
sites/<SITE>/{cards,curation,reports}/ product cards, Opus traces/proposals/review.md, reports
work/state.sqlite                      journal: files, listings, uploads, avu_desired, avu_journal,
                                       batches, site_runs
work/ontology_cache.duckdb             OLS term cache, taxa/unit/NLCD/biome maps, curation results
logs/                                  run/<SITE>/<stage>.log, sweep-<UTC>.log, status.json
```

The Data Store mirrors everything except `.venv`, `work/`, `logs/` and the raw harvest landings;
see [The published collection](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/data/collection/).

## Module map

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| `harvest.py`, `seal.py`, `flatten.py`, `catalog_lake.py` | Phase 1: fetch, seal, flatten (table specs in `flatten.TABLES`), build |
| `site/plan.py`, `site/fetch.py`, `site/stack.py`, `site/h5.py` | Phase 2 planning, listing and download, stacking, HDF5 |
| `site/terms.py`, `site/cards.py`, `site/curate.py`, `site/validate.py` | Ontology mapping, cards, Opus curation, OLS validation |
| `site/avus.py`, `avu/vocab.py`, `avu/bulk.py` | Desired AVUs for sites and the catalog; the journaled bulk writer |
| `avu/history.py`, `avu/recorder.py` | MESA history: direct and spool backends; the spool recorder |
| `mirror.py`, `site/upload.py` | Checksum-verified uploads; the versioned site-lake catalog |
| `site/stream.py`, `site/chunks.py`, `run.py`, `worker.py`, `coord.py`, `journal_sync.py` | Streaming, orchestration, multi-VM claims and journal backups |
| `verify_catalog.py`, `verify_site.py`, `verify_mesa.py` | Verification |

Interfaces between modules are fixed in [CONTRACTS](https://idss-mesa.github.io/neon-ducklake/CONTRACTS/). Where the design records
disagree, SCALING, CONTRACTS, STREAMING and RUNBOOK win over PLAN, and STREAMING wins on
streaming and multi-VM questions.
